top_story: A Saudi coalition strike that killed a 14-year-old girl on a school bus in Yemen on 8 October signaled a broader battlefield relapse, and within two days the conflict spilled sharply into Saudi territory when a Houthi attack on Riyadh airport killed 12 people and wounded more than 300. A second strike on King Khalid airport on 11 October, killing one and injuring 11, showed the first attack had not restored deterrence and instead deepened pressure in Riyadh for a harder military response, potentially with U.S. backing. That same day, a migrant boat carrying people toward Yemen capsized off Djibouti, leaving at least 139 dead and 84 missing, underscoring how war and economic desperation still pull civilians into lethal movement across the Red Sea. The regional picture is one of rapid escalation around Yemen in which reciprocal attacks are widening the civilian toll far beyond the front lines.
